text.aura: What you radiate is a freshly forged blade: sharp, clean and impossible to ignore. Gyeong carries a strong, direct presence that people feel the moment you enter. You read as confident, decisive and a little bit fearless, the person who would handle the emergency while everyone else is still panicking. Your glow is bold and uncompromising. Some people find it thrilling, others find it intimidating, and both reactions are a sign of power. There's also an unexpected loyalty in your energy, a protective edge that makes the right people feel completely safe. The glow-up for you isn't becoming softer to be liked. It's adding warmth so the strength reads as protective rather than cutting, a blade in a velvet sheath.
text.how-people-read-you: The snap judgment: strong, blunt, maybe intimidating. People assume you're tough, confident and not easily impressed, and they often hesitate before approaching. Once they know you, they find a fiercely loyal friend with surprising sentimentality and a strong sense of justice. The misreading comes from your directness. Some people think you're harsh when you're just efficient, or that you don't care when you simply don't fuss. Your resting expression can read as stern. A few small shifts change everything: soften your eyes when you listen, add a "how are you?" before getting to the point, and laugh more openly. You don't need to dilute your honesty. Just let people see the warm hand holding the sword.
text.colors: Your natural palette is bold Metal: crisp white, steel gray, silver, pewter, cool black. These make you look sharp, modern and powerful, like a well-cut suit. Earth supports Metal in the five elements, so camel, sand and taupe add warmth and approachability without losing strength. A camel coat over a white shirt is your aura in its best form. For softness, a touch of Water colors, deep navy or charcoal, works beautifully. Silver jewelry is your natural match, and chunkier pieces suit your strong energy. Hot red or orange works best as a single flash, a scarf or a lip. A whole outfit of it can make your already intense presence feel aggressive. Your colors should look clean, cool and confident.
text.style: Your best style is sharp minimalism. Tailored blazers, crisp shirts, structured coats, straight-leg trousers, clean sneakers or sleek boots. You look best in clear silhouettes with strong lines: nothing frilly, nothing fussy. A monochrome outfit looks incredible on you. The trap is going so severe that you look unapproachable or like you're dressed for a board meeting at a birthday party. Add one soft element per outfit: a cashmere knit, a silk scarf, a flowing fabric, a playful sock. Hair neat and clean-cut, grooming polished. Your best photo is in strong, clear light, urban backdrop, facing the camera directly with a slight, confident smile. You don't need to pose. You just need to let your presence speak.
text.vibe: Aim for this vibe: the protector with a soft heart. Picture the cold, competent K-drama lead who is secretly the warmest person in the story. Your evolution is showing that warmth sooner. Try saying the kind thing first, before the critique. Ask questions instead of giving verdicts. Let someone else win an argument that doesn't matter. Show your sentimental side, keep the ticket stub, frame the photo, tell people they matter. Wear something unexpectedly soft. These shifts don't weaken you. They make your strength trustworthy. People will still respect you, but they'll also feel safe approaching you, and that's when your aura becomes truly magnetic instead of just impressive.
text.aura-dims: People see you fade when you're battle-worn. You've been fighting too many fights, at work, in your head, on behalf of other people, and your edge turns brittle. You look tense, sound clipped and might snap at small things. Your style can become harsh and rigid too: all black, all armor, no softness anywhere. The reset is putting the sword down for a while. Do something physical and simple, like a long walk or cleaning out a cupboard. Spend time with someone who makes you laugh and needs nothing from you. Wear something soft and comfortable. Clear your space, because clutter bothers you more than most souls. Let one problem stay unsolved for a day. Even the strongest blade needs time in its sheath.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, your aura is a sword. Strong, clean, people trust you in a crisis.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: They also hesitate before saying hello. You look like you're about to fire them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Camel coat, white shirt, silver ring. Pure power, no effort.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: All black every day is not a personality. It's a uniform.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is the soft heart behind the armor.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Same sword, softer eyes. People lean in. That's it. Huge difference.

spring.intro: Spring gives a Gyeong blade a whole forest of Wood to cut, since Metal controls Wood, so your aura is purposeful, energetic and slightly intimidating. You read as decisive and capable, ready to fix whatever is broken before lunch. Your style tends to sporty, functional or utilitarian, built for action rather than charm, with a lot of pockets. Your glow-up is polish. Earth is your resource, so camel, sand and warm stone give your edge a grounded, expensive finish, and a single statement in steel or silver keeps your Metal clear. Try one tailored piece that still lets you move. The spring Gyeong glow looks like a well-made tool: functional, beautiful and obviously quality.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gyeong, cargo pockets aren't a personality. Camel trench, steel watch. Same energy, better finish.

summer.intro: Summer's Fire is the element that controls Metal, so a summer Gyeong is iron in the forge, and your aura reads as intense, resilient and impossible to bend. People sometimes see you as tough before they see you as kind. In the heat your style can harden too: black on black, heavy boots, sharp lines everywhere, like you are expecting a fight. Your glow-up is cooling and grounding. Earth bridges Fire and Metal, so taupe, stone and sand soften your edges, and Water blues cool the forge. Add white or silver for a clean, confident finish. The summer Gyeong glow is tempered steel: still strong, now with a beautiful sheen on it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gyeong, stone linen and a silver cuff. Still tough, now with a gorgeous sheen.

autumn.intro: An autumn birthday doubles your Metal, so a Gyeong aura born then is the blade at full sharpness. You read as confident, principled and a little severe. You likely love clean monochrome, structured coats and minimal jewelry, and you look excellent in all of it. The risk is coldness, because too much Metal reads as unapproachable. Your glow-up is warmth and flow. Fire refines Metal, so a deep red, warm burgundy or rust adds life, and Water, your output, brings fluid fabrics and inky blues that soften the structure. Wear one piece that moves, like silk or a loose knit. The autumn Gyeong glow is a polished blade wrapped in velvet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gyeong, the monochrome is flawless and slightly terrifying. A burgundy silk scarf makes it human.

winter.intro: Winter draws Water out of Metal, the element that produces it, so a winter Gyeong aura is cold steel in a river: sharp, reserved and quietly drained. You come across as cool and self-sufficient, maybe more distant than you mean to be. Your wardrobe likely runs dark and functional, the coat you bought because it was sensible. Your glow-up is warmth and support. Earth, your resource, brings camel, oatmeal and chestnut, which make you look grounded instead of guarded. Fire, which refines Metal, adds a flash of red or warm gold. A camel coat over a black base with one warm accent changes everything. The winter Gyeong glow is a blade gleaming by the fireplace.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gyeong, a camel coat over black, one red detail. Guarded becomes grounded.

earth.intro: A Gyeong Metal born in the Earth days is ore still inside the mountain: strong, steady and not yet fully shown. People read you as tough and reliable, sometimes a bit closed. Earth feeds Metal, but too much of it buries the shine, and heavy browns can make you look harder than you are. Your glow-up is clarity. Water washes Metal clean, so navy and cool blue work beautifully, and crisp white shows the edge. One polished metal accessory finishes it. The Earth-days Gyeong glow is steel catching light.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Gyeong, swap the brown for navy and let the steel show.

strength.strong: A strong Gyeong Metal aura is a blade in full sunlight. With plenty of Metal and Earth, you seem powerful, decisive and slightly intimidating, and your style can lean armored: sharp tailoring, black on black, heavy hardware on every strap. The blind spot is armor that overpowers. People respect you on sight but hesitate to approach or make a joke. Add Water for flow and Fire for warmth: a deep blue silk, a soft knit, a rust or burgundy accent. Your strength doesn't need to be worn on every inch of the outfit. Let one confident piece say it and let the rest relax.
strength.weak: A weak Gyeong Metal aura is a dulled sword that still remembers being sharp. With little Metal or Earth support, you may dress in tired, practical clothes that undersell how capable you are. The blind spot is shrinking into function: you look like someone who helps, not someone who leads. Your glow-up is structure. A crisp white shirt, a sharp blazer, a silver watch or cuff that you actually wear on weekdays. Choose clean lines that announce competence before you speak. People will start treating you like the leader you already are, and you will feel it.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
